$m\lceil n\alpha \rceil - n \lfloor m\alpha \rfloor = k$.
Since $\alpha$ is irrational, we have $\lceil x \rceil = \lfloor x \rfloor + 1$ for any $x = n\alpha$ (where $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$). Thus, the condition becomes:
$m(\lfloor n\alpha \rfloor + 1) - n \lfloor m\alpha \rfloor = k \implies m \lfloor n\alpha \rfloor + m - n \lfloor m\alpha \rfloor = k$.
Let $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ be the fractional part of $x$. The condition can be rewritten as:
$m(n\alpha - \{n\alpha\}) + m - n(m\alpha - \{m\alpha\}) = k$
$mn\alpha - m\{n\alpha\} + m - nm\alpha + n\{m\alpha\} = k$
$m + n\{m\alpha\} - m\{n\alpha\} = k \implies n\{m\alpha\} + m(1 - \{n\alpha\}) = k$.
